added_failure_note: A figure review runs no suite; the reviewed run's gate log is cited by that run's own manifest and is not re-measured here.
attachment_note: The three named PNGs were opened and read as images and nothing else was opened: no SVG, and no image besides them. Each verdict was formed from the pixels of those PNGs, and every measurement quoted in the findings and rubric lines was taken from those same pixels. Attribution to the three committed figures is by content and each match is unique: the residual strip draws every trip its frame reached and marks the current trip with the red dot, so the 5-point strip with the mark at trip 2 (image-0) is frame 137 trip 2 while the two 3-point strips are the frame-146 panels; the mark is at trip 1 in image-1 and trip 2 in image-2; and image-2 alone carries no 'bounding surface' legend entry, which the run's own manifest records as the trip-2 panel where no surface is drawn. The identically-shaped attachments were independently mapped the same way by the earlier figure review at head 5c04a6919.

rubric.data_ink: fail: the blue block carries no readable level information and the reference holds the core's weight (finding 1)
rubric.label_collision: pass for text; the band is cut flat at the axes top limit (finding 1)
rubric.legibility: fail: the solved field is a solid band above the limiter and absent in the core (finding 1)

findings.summary: The solved-flux contours render as a solid block instead of separable lines. In the rendered PNG the blue is a single contiguous run 31-33 px wide at rows y=120..150 with no white gap anywhere in it, against 3-5 px runs separated by white in both sibling panels. The nine shared levels are drawn at 3.0 pt (scripts/prototypes/diiid_vertical_loss/render_trip_panels.py:429, 4.2 px at 110 dpi), so where the field is nearly flat they crowd closer than one line width and fuse. The reader cannot read a single contour level in the region above the limiter, which is exactly where this panel's claim (the field collapsed, the axis lifted) sits, and the same merge recurs along the bottom edge. A block of colour carries no level information; either draw the crowded sets thinner or draw the envelope and a zoom.

The plasma core carries no solved-flux ink at all: in the core box x 680..800, y 210..430 the PNG holds 0 blue px against 6359 grey EFIT px, where the sibling panels hold 4533/2585 and 4373/2312. The two-field comparison the legend promises is therefore unavailable inside this panel, and with the reference now at 2.4 pt against the subject's 3.0 pt the core reads as an EFIT-only plot with a blue block above it. The absence is itself the reported collapse and the caption states it, so nothing is misread, but a reader can take the all-grey body for a rendering omission; one clause in the caption, or a thinner reference, would prevent that.

The solved X-point callout fuses with its own leader dot and nearly touches the solved axis. In the rendered PNG the red components measure 15x9 px (the X and the hollow dot at its true position, y 352..366) and 10x10 px (the axis triangle, y 370..379), the two 3 px apart. The callout fixed the saddle-against-axis crowding, but the saddle itself now reads at 1:1 as an undifferentiated red mark rather than the X the legend names, so the one mark that tells a reader the field has an interior saddle is the least legible mark on the panel.

The poloidal panel occupies 239 px of the 1400 px canvas width while the residual strip beneath it spans 1294 px, so about 83% of the width on either side of the contours is blank and the field is drawn at a fifth of the available size. On the served page at roughly 900 px wide the panel is about 154 px, which puts the hollow EFIT null markers at about 5 px. Nothing is clipped or hidden, and the artifact is a vector figure a reader can enlarge, but the layout spends the canvas on emptiness instead of on the geometry the figure exists to show: placing the strip beside the panel would give the contours about 1.5x the drawn height on the same page.

The strip labels the same quantity to two different precisions across the set: this panel ticks '0.0' and '0.1' while both frame-146 panels tick '0.00' and '0.25', because the residual axis takes matplotlib's automatic locator and formatter per panel range and no formatter is set (scripts/prototypes/diiid_vertical_loss/render_trip_panels.py:618). Each panel is correct on its own, but a reader comparing the three must notice that both the step and the precision changed before the marks can be compared.
